summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx and techworx (pages) site projects by mining ~810 sessions, then act on the findings (exploration mode, gate hygiene, planner, routing, path fixes) and trim expensive model tiers.
summary.outcome: Four parallel tracks (gate hygiene ADR 013, outcome-level plans ADR 014, skill routing, measurement) plus a CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT path rewrite and version bumps (ecosystem 4.5.0) were merged and pushed as draft PR #21 (Entire trail #290), and the fable and astra tiers were then replaced with opus and gpt-6.1-sol; Antigravity behavior and post-release testing are left to the user.

repo: The corpus was smaller than first counted: the orin-dx project dir has only 2 real sessions and pages ~7 top-level sessions; the rest of the ~810 files are subagent transcripts.

Plugin agents were used in only a few sessions (orin-dx b8d16e96 and pages 24655582, plus one vanguard run); all design ideation ran through Artifacts, forks, general-purpose agents and local dev server screenshots.
Plugin pipeline is spec-driven with default-fail gates and has no sketch/spike/explore mode, no visual/browser capability, and spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout or appearance.
muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist, so implemented a11y was never checked.

Gates caught real behavioral defects (contrast ratios, cross-spec contradictions, stale breakpoints) but missed visual defects; later wording-only blockers caused churn, e.g. SPEC-001 needed 13 verdicts and eight specs took 51 gate calls.
The orchestrator ignored the gate's 3-retry cap and escalation (SPEC-005 retry 4, SPEC-008 retry 7) and carried on without asking the user.

Relative shared/... paths in skills and agents fail on first read because shared is a symlink; ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/... is substituted in skills and agents and reads first time (single-run evidence, Claude Code only). 163 references in 66 files were rewritten; Codex sources unchanged.
plan@1 never required code in tasks, so no schema change was needed for outcome-level plans; the 'exact code' text is only in two stale description strings.
The constitution block is copied byte-for-byte into every agent (ADR 006), so gate rules were placed in each gate's <output> instead.

Fable (claude-fable-5-1) was used only by scribe:arch-auditor and scribe:architect and astra only by the Codex judge role; both cost about 2x the next tier down and were chosen by position, not measurement.
Merge conflicts across parallel worktree tracks were confined to docs/evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md and docs/adr/README.md and were resolved by keeping both sides.

code.finding: Defines the cognitive tier model with no divergent/exploratory mode; the fable row was removed in the final tier change.
Smith accepts a spec@1 with no plan, but still runs recon, mutator, reviewer and a binding exit-gate; there is no spike mode.

workflow: Delegating investigation to parallel background agents (plugin inventory, two session analyses, outcome audit) worked well, but their counts needed correction against the actual corpus; treat subagent reports as unverified until checked.
Visual option boards and rendered prototypes were what let the user decide; text-first descriptions repeatedly forced 'show me' requests.
Probe plugins with single-variable controls were an effective way to test host behavior such as path substitution.
Checking changelog claims against the actual diff before applying version bumps caught inaccurate statements.
Pushing and opening a PR required explicit user approval; the user's 'recommendations look good' was treated as that go-ahead.
Entire auto-linked a trail (#290) to the PR branch, so no manual trail creation was needed.

friction: Initial session count (~810 sessions) was misleading because most files were subagent transcripts.
Agents stalled on 60-130 KB spec and plan files; 17 failed agent tasks and 32 stalled mentions were observed in the sessions.
Gate loops churned on wording-only blockers, and some blockers were caused by the previous round's prescribed fix.
The user could not judge specs in prose and had to repeatedly ask for visual examples; width and other decisions were lost across sessions.
Specs lagged behind prototypes and were retrofitted; SPEC-013 superseded 26 SPEC-001 criteria and 35 of 36 SPEC-003c criteria.
Repo-wide pre-commit gate caused waits during parallel smith runs.
A GPG-signed merge commit needed the sandbox disabled in a worktree.
Ranger's first live exit-gate run was denied once by the hook and the denial reason was not recorded.
Relative shared/ paths failed on first read in live probes, and the first planner runs invented schema-forbidden task keys because the temp project lacked shared/schemas.
open_items: Antigravity: verify whether it substitutes ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in skill and agent text and how it follows the shared symlink (user will check later).
Review and accept ADRs 011-014; ADR 014 (partially supersedes ADR 009) rests on one fixture and one run each.
PR #21 / trail #290 still need human approval; no trail description has been set.
Gate retry path past round one and outcome-level plans with real implementers have not been run live; savings in gate rounds, turns and tokens are unmeasured (docs/evaluation-runbook.md).
Retry rule is softer: defects missed in round one can pass on a retry as non-blocking gaps.
Sentinel and ranger got patch bumps although gates can now deny previously passing reports; the user may prefer minor.
Impact of dropping fable and astra on boundary-conflict and binding-verdict catches is unmeasured; record in assumptions register as 'Open: measure' and restore tiers if misses appear.
Ranger exit-gate may need the context.md load_first line, and hook denial reasons should be added to the trace.
Remaining courier gap: Callisto's flat .changeset/ markdown format (D6), and the Callisto repo AGENTS.md/PR template should point to courier skills.
Missing capabilities identified: sketch/explore mode, visual render and screenshot gating, spec-from-prototype path, cross-session decision memory, a11y taxonomy in ranger.
